tickets.title: Coordinate Divorce Planning Documents
tickets.text:
Use this workflow to request, organize, and route divorce-related planning documents for analysis. Keep communications neutral and factual, confirm authorization before sharing information with outside professionals, and separate advisory planning needs from legal advice.

Coordinate with attorney Corin Nettlewhisk and CPA Jules Thimblefern after written authorization. The planning packet should cover draft settlement terms, asset schedules, support estimates, retirement-account order questions, and current statements.

subTasks.title: Confirm document scope and permissions
subTasks.text: Identify which documents are needed, such as draft or final settlement terms, asset schedules, support obligations, retirement account orders, tax returns, and current statements. Confirm the client’s written permission before coordinating with an attorney, CPA, or mediator.

subTasks.title: Create secure collection folder
subTasks.text: Set up a secure upload location, list missing items, and label received documents by category. Do not request or store unnecessary sensitive documents beyond the planning scope.

subTasks.title: Prepare planning summary for advisor review
subTasks.text: Summarize available assets, liabilities, income obligations, beneficiary concerns, account titling issues, and open questions for the advisor. Flag any urgent implementation constraints without providing legal conclusions.

tickets.evidence: They agreed by 2026-07-17 to coordinate with attorney Corin Nettlewhisk and CPA Jules Thimblefern after written authorization, with a planning packet covering draft settlement terms, asset schedules, support estimates, retirement-account order questions, and current statements.

tickets.title: Collect Client Tax Documents
tickets.text:
Request and organize current tax documents for planning review, including prior-year federal and state returns, W-2s, 1099s, K-1s, estimated tax payment records, charitable giving summaries, and any tax notices. Track missing items and route complete packet to the planning team.

Obtain the most recent joint return, latest property tax bill, and current Teacup Comet Bank mortgage payoff for Nadia Pebblefizz’s cash-flow and basis review. Current brokerage statements and pay stubs are already in the secure folder.
tickets.evidence: the most recent joint return, latest property tax bill, and current Teacup Comet Bank mortgage payoff are still needed by 2026-07-15

tickets.title: Review Account Security Follow-Up Evidence
tickets.text:
Review the account security follow-up using these criteria and collect supporting evidence:

Criteria:
- Confirm the client’s identity was verified through approved procedures.
- Determine whether the concern involved password reset, suspicious login, changed contact information, failed multi-factor authentication, or unauthorized transaction risk.
- Verify whether any account access, banking instructions, beneficiary data, or contact details changed recently.
- Confirm the custodian or platform security team has been notified when required.
- Check whether trading, money movement, or profile changes should remain restricted until cleared.
- Document the client’s preferred secure contact method for future updates.

Evidence to collect:
- Internal note of identity verification steps completed.
- Timestamped summary of client report or advisor observation.
- Custodian case number or secure message reference, if available.
- Screenshots or alerts only when policy allows secure storage.
- Confirmation of password reset, MFA update, or access restoration.
- Final disposition and any remaining monitoring instructions.

Review Nadia Pebblefizz’s IRA beneficiary record against Corin Nettlewhisk’s temporary restrictions before any beneficiary change is submitted. The last record still names Rowan Pebblefizz. Elena completed identity verification and restored secure portal access on 2026-07-06 after multi-factor authentication failed on Nadia’s replacement phone.
